name: Horse chestnut extract
description: Horse chestnut extract (CAS 8053-39-2 ), derived from Aesculus hippocastanum, is a standardized botanical extract valued across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic supply chains. Standardized primarily to escin content, it delivers measurable active concentration for formulators requiring consistent batch performance. Procurement typically targets defined escin levels to meet finished product specifications. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into oral dosage forms such as capsules, tablets, and soft gels targeting venous health and circulatory support. Topical pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulators use it in creams, gels, and serums where antioxidant activity and skin-conditioning performance are required. In personal care, it appears in anti-aging and firming formulations where botanical actives with documented activity are commercially preferred. Food supplement producers also source it for functional beverage and powder blend applications where standardized botanical extracts are a label-active ingredient. This versatility makes it a staple for manufacturers looking for reliable botanical performance across diverse product lines. Horse chestnut extract is supplied as a dry powder, typically standardized to 20% or 40% escin by HPLC. Liquid and hydroglycolic extract forms are available for direct cosmetic incorporation depending on the specific formulation requirements of the end user. Grades include cosmetic-grade and food supplement-grade material, with specifications aligned to Ph. Eur. monograph requirements where applicable.
